newsitem.title: USA: Cunanan did not have AIDS - Miami Herald.
newsitem.headline: Cunanan did not have AIDS - Miami Herald.

text.p: Andrew Cunanan, suspected killer of fashion king Gianni Versace, was not infected with the AIDS virus when he killed himself aboard a Miami Beach houseboat, the Miami Herald reported on Friday.

The newspaper said three law enforcement sources told them, on condition of anonymity, that tests performed on Cunanan's body at Dade County Medical Examiner's Office after his July 23 death showed he was not HIV positive.

There has been widespread speculation that Cunanan, a 27-year-old homosexual prostitute, launched a cross-country murder spree upon learning that he had contracted the AIDS virus. Versace, slain in Miami Beach on July 15, is believed to have been Cunanan's fifth victim.
State Attorney Katherine Fernandez Rundle declined to confirm or deny the report.

"Florida statutes do not permit me or my office, without a court order, to confirm or deny that an HIV test has been performed on any person, or to disclose any such test results, if they exist," she said in a statement.
"Additionally, my office remains in the process of determining whether it will request a court to order the disclosure of any such test results."
The Herald's report quoted Rundle as saying that if the AIDS test was negative "then it certainly would eliminate the speculation as to his motivation on those grounds."
Cunanan committed suicide on the houseboat moored 40 blocks from the Versace muder site. The body was found by police who stormed the boat.
